cards.text: Meet Micah the Moreshite. The word of the LORD comes to him in the days of THREE kings of Judah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, and what he sees is about Samaria and Jerusalem. Three kings and he's still on the job, while I worked ONE kitchen and got slid into a junk drawer.
Micah doesn't ease into this one. No small talk, he opens LOUD, like a phone alarm at 5 a.m. with the volume ALL the way up.

cards.question: Micah calls all peoples to hear, and the whole ___ to listen.

cards.text: Then Micah says, "May the Lord GOD bear witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple." Witness AGAINST you, friend, and that is NOT a glowing job reference.
And behold, the LORD comes forth from His dwelling place, and He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth. Trust me, friend, nobody's hitting snooze on THAT alarm.

cards.question: When the LORD comes down and treads on the high places of the earth, what will the mountains beneath Him do?
Micah says the valleys will hold firm while the mountains melt.
Melting mountains and splitting valleys. Micah says all this is because of what?

cards.text: Then Micah asks what the transgression of Jacob is, and points right at a city: "Is it not Samaria?" Then he asks about the high place of Judah: "Is it not Jerusalem?"

Now the LORD speaks: He'll make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, with her stones poured into the valley and her foundations exposed. That's not a remodel, friend, that's the whole house down to the dirt.

cards.question: Once Samaria is rubble in the open field, what does the LORD say the spot will become?

answers.text: A planting area for a vineyard
A pasture for flocks of sheep
A camp for an army of soldiers

cards.question: Along with the city itself, the LORD says He will destroy all of Samaria's ___.

cards.text: ALL of Samaria's carved images will be smashed to pieces, and ALL her wages burned in the fire. Then the LORD says, "Since she collected the wages of a prostitute, they will be used again on a prostitute."

cards.question: Because of what's coming for Samaria, Micah says he will lament and wail.

cards.text: Micah says he'll walk barefoot and naked, howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich. I think this one hurts him deep.

cards.question: Micah says Samaria's wound has spread as far as Jerusalem.

cards.text: Now Micah's lament goes town by town, from Gath to Adullam, like a roll call where nobody wants to hear their name. One town is told to roll in the dust, another to depart in shameful nakedness, and Micah says to send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath. Lachish is called the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion, and calamity came down from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem.

cards.question: At the end of the lament, Micah tells his listeners to shave themselves bald and cut off their hair. Why?

answers.text: To keep a vow to the LORD

cards.question: Micah gives the reason for all that mourning: the precious children will go into ___.
